_README: Allowlist for tools/golden/reach.py. Every entry is a connection that is
*absent on purpose*; docs/bindings/REACH.md is the inventory and the argument.
Matched exactly, in both directions. An unlisted gap fails the suite, and an
entry whose gap has since closed fails it too -- so closing a gap deletes its
entry in the same change and this file always describes the present.
`reason` is prose for the reader. `upstream_absent` / `upstream_present` are
for the checker: attribute paths on real upstream torch that the reason is
staking itself on, verified by `reach.py --verify-upstream` (a subprocess
with PYTHONPATH stripped). A reason nobody can put a question to is how
docs/bindings/SPELLINGS.md's deliberate gaps would otherwise become indistinguishable

aten._fft_c2r.default.reason: Upstream has `torch._fft_c2r` (it is a `_VariableFunctions` member) but no `Tensor._fft_c2r`, and this shim deliberately does NOT put a row in `overloads.json` for it. The reason is not that upstream lacks the door -- it is that the door nobody uses is not the one that reaches this kernel: `torch.fft.rfft`/`fft`/`ifft`/`irfft` are C++-level composites that land on `aten::_fft_c2r` through the dispatcher, and `torch.stft` reaches it through `aten::stft`, which IS spelled and IS exercised. Adding `torch._fft_c2r` would add a spelling with no measured caller, which docs/bindings/SPELLINGS.md prices as surface. The kernel is proven element-wise against a live upstream in `pytests/test_fft.py` and, through `aten.stft.*`, by the golden harness. Delete this entry if a caller for the bare spelling is found.

The reason is not that upstream lacks the door -- it is that the door nobody uses is not the one that reaches this kernel: `torch.fft.rfft`/`fft`/`ifft`/`irfft` are C++-level composites that land on `aten::_fft_r2c` through the dispatcher, and `torch.stft` reaches it through `aten::stft`, which IS spelled and IS exercised. Adding `torch._fft_r2c` would add a spelling with no measured caller, which docs/bindings/SPELLINGS.md prices as surface. The kernel is proven element-wise against a live upstream in `pytests/test_fft.py` and, through `aten.stft.*`, by the golden harness. Delete this entry if a caller for the bare spelling is found.

aten.alias.default.reason: Upstream exposes no `torch.alias` and no `Tensor.alias` -- `aten::alias` is a dispatcher-internal view op that upstream's own Python surface never names. Inventing a spelling for it would be exactly what docs/bindings/SPELLINGS.md refuses (a door upstream does not have). The kernel is reached, and needs to be, through `_aten_dispatch` from traced/exported graphs and through the vendored `__getitem__`'s view path.

aten.lift_fresh_copy.default.reason: Upstream exposes no `torch.lift_fresh_copy` and no `Tensor.lift_fresh_copy` (measured on 2.13.0, alongside `alias` above, which is the same shape). `aten::lift_fresh_copy` is what functionalisation REWRITES `aten::lift_fresh` into, so it is reached from a traced/exported graph and from nowhere else -- `docs/graph/LIFTFRESH.md` §1.2 measures that `lift_fresh` never survives into an exported graph and this op always does. Inventing a `torch.<name>` for it would be exactly the door upstream does not have that docs/bindings/SPELLINGS.md refuses. The kernel is compared element-wise against upstream by the golden harness (21 cases over 7 dtypes and 3 shapes) and end-to-end through a real `torch.export` in `pytests/test_liftfresh.py`, which exports a module holding Python literals, replays it and asserts the operator is in the graph. Delete this entry if a caller for a bare spelling is found.
